title: Describing Smooth Block Collection
text:
I'm now diving into *Video H*, focusing on a unique gameplay approach. I've noted the player, `[GD]`, methodically building a perfectly smooth, symmetrical block with a dark background. The player carefully aligns individual blocks around the core, achieving a seamless outer layer (121 score). I've observed his interaction with other players and the precise use of obstacles for refinement. Finally, I've noted a network interruption as he approaches large, final blocks.


**Observing Video H Gameplay**

I'm now detailing *Video H*'s gameplay. I've noted the opening segment with `Jelly`, includi
A player spawns as a single 1x1 square gem block with their nickname displayed across their main/core block.
Touching small stray 1x1 blocks floating on the map attaches them to the player's block structure at the point of contact on a grid alignment.
When attached blocks form a complete solid square (e.g., 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, up to giant squares), they automatically merge into a single larger glossy gem block.
Players can build complex multi-block structures with multiple merged squares of varying sizes or hollow ring shapes attached to their core block.
In the later update (Feb 2017 / mobile release), the player's core block is represented by a specific 2x2-sized Heart Block marked with a heart icon, rather than the largest merged block.
The player's block cluster moves continuously toward the mouse cursor position on PC (or virtual directional arrow on mobile).
Pressing A rotates the player's block cluster counter-clockwise and pressing D rotates it clockwise.
Rotating with A or D consumes energy from the vertical green bar on the bottom-left and grants a temporary movement/rotational speed boost.
In the later update (Video D), rotating/spinning causes unmerged 1x1 outer blocks to detach and fall off the player's structure.
Pressing W shoots/ejects a 1x1 block from the player's structure toward the cursor, which also consumes a small amount of the green energy bar.
In the initial version (Videos A, B, C, E, F, H), shooting blocks with W can break down the player's own main block into smaller blocks to regain high movement speed.
Movement speed decreases as the player's main block / total mass grows larger.
The camera is top-down 2D, centered on the player's core block, and dynamically zooms out as the player's block structure grows larger.
When two players collide, larger blocks destroy smaller blocks on contact, shattering them into collectible 1x1 blocks.
In the initial version, a player dies immediately if their main (named) block is destroyed by a larger enemy block; losing outer/secondary blocks does not kill the player.
In the later Heart Block update (Video D), a player dies if and only if their Heart Block is destroyed.
White/grey square obstacle blocks are scattered throughout the arena and form a continuous perimeter wall around the map.

If a player's outer/secondary block touches a white obstacle block, that block explodes/shatters into small 1x1 blocks; if the player's main/core block touches a white obstacle block in the early version, the player dies or their main block
If a white obstacle block is hit enough times, it is destroyed and disappears from the map.

In the later update (Video D), large neutral colored gem blocks ('food blocks') spawn around the map; players with sufficiently large blocks can ram them to shatter them into a cluster of collectible 1x1 blocks.
Each 1x1 block attached to the player's structure equals 1 point of score, which is tracked in real time on the leaderboard.
In the later update (Video D), large players experience slow score decay (losing approximately 1 block per second) to prevent passive camping.

The HUD displays a 4-quadrant minimap in the top-left showing player dots, a vertical green energy/power bar (0 to 100) in the bottom-left, and a Top 10 leaderboard plus the player's current rank and score in the top-right.

Players can select free cosmetic skins (solid colors or YouTuber/creator logos such as Kwebbelkop, MasterOv, Jelly, Slogoman, AzzyLand, FaZe Mojo) from the Skin menu, which apply to every merged square block in their structure.
The settings menu allows players to toggle a Dark Background theme and select a server region (Europe Frankfurt/London, N. America East/Central/West/South, Asia Tokyo/Singapore).
The game supports cross-platform multiplayer between web browsers (PC) and mobile devices (iOS/Android), as well as Party codes (Create/Join) and Free For All / Teams modes.
In the later update (Video D), popping/collecting sound effects play when picking up small blocks or shattering large blocks.

title: Upgrading Cluster.js
text:
I'm currently focused on upgrading `public/js/cluster.js`, specifically tackling Issue 2, which involves steering, rotation pivots, and wall clamping anchored to the main core block. I've begun by modifying the `rebuildSquares()` function to address these requirements. I'm carefully analyzing the logic to ensure a robust solution.


**Centering Core Square**

I've been working on ensuring the core square remains centered at (0,0). I'm implementing a check that detects if the core square drifts from (0,0) when not in `heartMode`. If it drifts, I'm shifting all cell keys, squares, and the object's world coordinates to bring the core square back to the center. I'm also adding `getCoreWorldCenter()` for precise world coordinate retrieval, critical for rotation pivots.


**Refining Steer & Clamping**

I've determined that placing the cursor to the right on screen will always steer right, given `dx` and `dy`. I'm also implementing perimeter wall clamping by checking the world bounding box of all squares against `wallLimit`, ensuring no clipping.

title: Upgrading Collisions System
text:
I'm currently focused on upgrading the collision detection system, particularly within `public/js/world.js`. My primary concern now is optimizing the caching of `CanvasPattern` objects to avoid redundant calls to `ctx.createPattern`. This should significantly improve performance, especially with complex world elements and AI interactions.


**Optimizing PvP Collisions**

I'm now integrating PvP collision detection within the `world.update` loop. I'm focusing on efficiently managing remote player data using proxy wrappers from the `net.players` data, which should significantly improve the gameplay experience. Specifically, I'm working to handle collisions between the local player and remote players within the `resolveRemoteCollision` function. This involves checking for overlap between player squares and implementing collision effects such as shattering.


**Implementing PvP Mechanics**

I've been working on PvP hit detection within the collision logic. I'm implementing different reactions based on square size. title: Reviewing Remaining Issues
text:
I'm now diving into `public/js/main.js` to eliminate the last few bugs. I've begun addressing Issue 10, specifically the `window.__events` overflow. I intend to remove the old, potentially problematic, overflow logic completely.


**Addressing Background Simulation**

I'm focusing now on background tab behavior for Issues 5 and 7. My solution incorporates a `setInterval` fallback to keep things moving. A timer checks `performance.now() - lastFrame` to ensure updates, and prevent freezing of occluded or background tabs. This addresses `requestAnimationFrame` timing issues to ensure `net.state(...)` is broadcasting regularly.


**Implementing PvP Features**

title: Analyzing Caching Behavior
text: I've discovered the root cause of the caching issue. It seems Chromium's in-memory script cache aggressively caches identical URLs across navigations. My solution is to include a version query parameter, like `?v=2`, in the script tags within `public/` to force cache invalidation.
